chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed by a woman in Ihram who had veiled herself with a hand fan, so he himself removed the hand fan from her face.

key_terms.مِحْرِمَة: A woman in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مِرْوَحَة: A hand fan, used here as a veil for the face

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam do when he saw a woman in Ihram using a hand fan to veil her face?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) personally removes the *mirwah* (a small hand fan) from a woman's face, providing a practical demonstration of the specific etiquette for female veiling during Ihram. This incident highlights the distinction between the face and the hands, reinforcing the scholarly view that while the face is covered, the *mirwah* serves as a specific, permissible tool for protection from sunlight and dust without being considered part of the face veil itself.
